quizName: DMV Practice Test #11 20 Questions • Passing Score 16

questions.question: Is braking in a turn easier or harder than braking on a straight road?

options.text: Easier than braking on a straight road.
Harder than braking on a straight road.
Safe only if you use the front brake.
Safe only if you use the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Harder than braking on a straight road.
questions.explanation: Braking in a turn is harder than braking on a straight road. You can use both brakes in a turn, but you must know the right technique and be very careful.

questions.question: Which item is NOT protective riding gear?

options.text: A leather jacket
Boots that cover your ankles
Hearing protection
Pants made of soft material

questions.correctAnswerText: Pants made of soft material
questions.explanation: Good protective gear includes a jacket and pants made of leather or sturdy material, boots that cover and support your ankles, and hearing protection even with a helmet.

questions.question: When should you wear reflective clothing?

options.text: Never
Only during the day
Only at night
During the day and at night

questions.correctAnswerText: During the day and at night
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day. Wear bright colors and reflective materials all the time to stay visible.

questions.question: Which one does NOT help reduce accident risk?

options.text: Staying alert
Spotting hazards and deciding which to handle first
Riding without a headlight
Keeping space around your motorcycle

questions.correctAnswerText: Riding without a headlight
questions.explanation: To lower your crash risk, stay alert and ready to react. Spot hazards and prioritize them. Always use your headlight to be more visible and keep plenty of space around your motorcycle.

questions.question: What is the best lane position?

options.text: Always the right side of the lane
Always the center of the lane
Always the left side of the lane
It depends on the road, weather, and traffic

questions.correctAnswerText: It depends on the road, weather, and traffic
questions.explanation: There is no one best lane position to always use. Change your lane position based on the road, weather, and traffic conditions.

questions.question: When riding behind a car, what should you do?

options.text: Position yourself so the driver can see you
Always ride on the far left side of the lane
Do not worry about your position
Always ride on the far right side of the lane

questions.correctAnswerText: Position yourself so the driver can see you
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane when behind a car. This position is most likely to show up in the driver's rearview mirror. Drivers look in their rearview mirror more often than their side mirrors.

questions.question: If a dog is chasing you, what should you do?

options.text: Kick it away
Stop and wait for it to lose interest
Swerve around it
Ride slowly toward it, then speed up

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride slowly toward it, then speed up
questions.explanation: If a dog chases you, slow down and approach it. Once you are close, speed up and leave it behind. Do not try to kick it.

questions.question: When riding in a group, what should riders do about space?

options.text: They do not need any space cushion
They should use more space than usual
They should use half their normal space
They should keep adequate space around each rider

questions.correctAnswerText: They should keep adequate space around each rider
questions.explanation: In a group, ride close together but still keep enough space around each rider for safety.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, how should you adjust?

options.text: Ride slower than normal
Stay closer to the car in front than you normally would
Ride faster than normal
Brake a little later than normal

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride slower than normal
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight, so your motorcycle needs more time to speed up, slow down, and turn. Ride slower, start braking earlier, leave more following distance, and look for bigger gaps when turning or merging.

questions.question: How should you sit for better motorcycle control?

options.text: Lean on your arms instead of steering
Keep your knees against the gas tank
Let your feet hang off the footrests
Sit far back so you have to stretch to reach the handlebars

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your knees against the gas tank
questions.explanation: Keep your knees against the gas tank for balance in turns. Sit close enough that your arms are slightly bent when holding the handlebars. Use your arms to steer, not to hold yourself up. Keep your feet firmly on the footrests.

questions.question: Where is the clutch lever usually located?

options.text: On the left handgrip
On the right handgrip
Near the left footrest
Near the right footrest

questions.correctAnswerText: On the left handgrip
questions.explanation: The clutch lever is on the left handgrip of a motorcycle.

questions.question: A three-wheeled motorcycle:

options.text: Handles curves about the same as a two-wheeled motorcycle.
Handles curves differently than a two-wheeled motorcycle.
Should not be operated in curves.
Should use the shoulder when taking a curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Handles curves differently than a two-wheeled motorcycle.
questions.explanation: A three-wheeled motorcycle or one with a sidecar handles curves differently than a two-wheeled motorcycle.

questions.question: To best control a motorcycle, a rider should:

options.text: Sit with their arms fully extended.
Use their arms to hold their body up.
Keep their knees away from the gas tank.
Keep their feet firmly on the footrests.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep their feet firmly on the footrests.
questions.explanation: Sit so your arms control the motorcycle, not hold your body up. Keep your arms slightly bent. Press your knees against the gas tank and keep your feet firmly on the footrests for balance.

questions.question: The front brake supplies how much of a motorcycle's stopping power?

options.text: About one-quarter
About one-half
About three-quarters
All the stopping power

questions.correctAnswerText: About three-quarters
questions.explanation: The front brake is stronger than the rear brake. It provides about three-quarters of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: If you are being chased by a dog, you should:

options.text: Kick it away.
Stop until the animal loses interest.
Swerve around the animal.
Approach the animal slowly, then speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Approach the animal slowly, then speed up.
questions.explanation: If a dog chases you, downshift and slow down as you approach it. Then accelerate and leave it behind.

questions.question: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield:

options.text: Is not necessary if you have a windshield.
Only protects your eyes.
Protects more than just your eyes.
Does not protect your face as well as goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protects more than just your eyes.
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your whole face, including your eyes. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield alone is not enough protection.

questions.question: You should check traffic behind your motorcycle especially:

options.text: Before starting into a curve.
When approaching an intersection.
When carrying a passenger.
Before slowing down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before slowing down.
questions.explanation: Always check your mirrors before you slow down. Drivers behind you may not expect you to slow down or may not see that you are slowing down.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger or cargo:

options.text: It may take less time to accelerate, but more time to stop.
It may take more time to accelerate and stop.
It may take more time to accelerate, but less time to stop.
It may take less time to accelerate and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: It may take more time to accelerate and stop.
questions.explanation: Extra weight from a passenger or cargo makes your motorcycle take longer to accelerate and longer to stop.

questions.question: Before riding, check all of the following, except:

options.text: Your tires' inflation pressure.
The amount of tread on your tires.
The reflective quality of your tires.
The general condition of the sidewalls on your tires.

questions.correctAnswerText: The reflective quality of your tires.
questions.explanation: Before every ride, check your tire pressure, tire tread, and the condition of the tire sidewalls and tread surface.

questions.question: Where is the greatest potential for conflict between a motorcycle and other traffic?

options.text: Intersections
Highways
Parking lots
Residential areas

questions.correctAnswerText: Intersections
questions.explanation: The greatest risk of conflict between your motorcycle and other traffic is at intersections. Be extra alert where another vehicle may cross your path.
